message:
## Vulnerability Digest

Seven relevant vulnerability developments were verified in the 24-hour scan window. The highest-priority items are the three new Erlang/OTP vulnerabilities and the ManageEngine ADSelfService Plus GINA-client issue. Several Ubuntu security notices and a Veeam threat update also warrant deployment checks.

**Scope**

- Sources: `Products.txt` and `List_of_SIA_Completed.txt` only; obvious aliases, capitalization variants, and duplicates were normalized.
- `DLL_software_component.txt` was not read or combined with this scan.
- Window: 2026-09-22 05:10 IST through 2026-09-23 05:10 IST (2026-09-21 23:40 UTC through 2026-09-22 23:40 UTC).

**Finding 1: Erlang/OTP TLS 1.3 certificate-validation bypass**

- Product: Erlang/OTP
- Issue: CVE-2026-89422
- Severity: Critical, CVSS 9.3
- Description: An unsolicited TLS 1.3 pre-shared-key extension can cause an Erlang TLS client to skip certificate and hostname validation, allowing a peer to impersonate the intended server.
- Relevance: Erlang/OTP is explicitly monitored and may underpin RabbitMQ deployments.
- Source: [Ubuntu CVE record](https://ubuntu.com/security/CVE-2026-89422); [Erlang/OTP 27.3.4.18 release](https://www.erlang.org/patches/OTP-27.3.4.18)

**Finding 2: Erlang/OTP ASN.1 denial of service**

- Product: Erlang/OTP
- Issue: CVE-2026-65634
- Severity: High, CVSS 8.2
- Description: Crafted oversized ASN.1 object identifiers can trigger excessive CPU use during certificate parsing before trust validation.
- Relevance: Direct match to Erlang/OTP; TLS clients and mutual-TLS servers that parse peer certificates may be exposed.
- Source: [Ubuntu CVE record](https://ubuntu.com/security/CVE-2026-65634); [Erlang/OTP 27.3.4.18 release](https://www.erlang.org/patches/OTP-27.3.4.18)

**Finding 3: Erlang/OTP SSH resource exhaustion**

- Product: Erlang/OTP
- Issue: CVE-2026-68956
- Severity: High, CVSS 7.1
- Description: An authenticated remote user can open unhandled SSH session channels until node memory is exhausted because the configured channel limit was not enforced.
- Relevance: Direct match to Erlang/OTP and relevant to deployments using its SSH application.
- Source: [Ubuntu CVE record](https://ubuntu.com/security/CVE-2026-68956); [Erlang/OTP 27.3.4.18 release](https://www.erlang.org/patches/OTP-27.3.4.18)

**Finding 4: ManageEngine ADSelfService Plus GINA-client RCE**

- Product: ManageEngine ADSelfService Plus
- Issue: CVE-2026-74849
- Severity: High per ManageEngine; NVD/GitHub currently score it Critical, CVSS 9.8
- Description: An unauthenticated attacker with access to the Windows logon screen may abuse the embedded GINA-client browser to execute code as SYSTEM. Builds 7000 and below are affected; build 7001 fixes the issue.
- Relevance: The monitored list contains ManageEngine. The affected subproduct should be confirmed in inventory.
- Freshness: The vendor fixed the issue on 24 August, but the CVE and NVD/GitHub records were published on 22 September.
- Source: [ManageEngine advisory](https://www.manageengine.com/products/self-service-password/advisory/CVE-2026-74849.html); [GitHub/NVD advisory record](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vwcx-qwxm-ffwg)

**Finding 5: Ubuntu OpenSSH security rollup**

- Product: Ubuntu OpenSSH
- Issues: CVE-2026-35386, CVE-2026-35387, CVE-2026-35414, CVE-2026-59995, CVE-2026-59997, CVE-2026-59998, CVE-2026-59999, CVE-2026-60000, CVE-2026-60001, CVE-2026-73282
- Severity: No aggregate severity stated by Canonical
- Description: Canonical issued fixes for command execution, authorization and forwarding bypasses, unsafe SFTP paths, authentication resource exhaustion, and a concurrent-forwarding use-after-free.
- Relevance: Direct matches to Ubuntu and OpenSSH. This notice applies to Ubuntu 14.04, 16.04, 18.04, and 20.04 LTS packages.
- Source: [Ubuntu USN-8804-1](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8804-1)

**Finding 6: Ubuntu libssh2 memory-safety issues**

- Product: Ubuntu libssh2
- Issues: CVE-2026-58050, CVE-2026-58051, CVE-2026-66032, CVE-2026-66034
- Severity: Not clearly stated by Canonical
- Description: Malicious SSH or SFTP servers can trigger crashes or possibly arbitrary code execution in libssh2 clients through malformed public-key attributes, list entries, or server responses.
- Relevance: Applies to monitored Ubuntu systems using libssh2 packages across Ubuntu 14.04 through 22.04 LTS.
- Source: [Ubuntu USN-8799-1](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8799-1)

**Finding 7: Veeam privilege-escalation threat update**

- Product: Veeam Agent for Microsoft Windows / Veeam Backup & Replication
- Issue: CVE-2026-32996
- Severity: CVSS 7.3; NHS threat severity Medium
- Description: NHS England published a new threat bulletin concerning public proof-of-concept code for a local privilege-escalation flaw that can yield SYSTEM privileges. The vulnerability itself was originally disclosed in May and the proof of concept on 14 September.
- Relevance: Veeam is explicitly monitored; the bulletin names Backup & Replication 13.0.1.2067 and earlier version 13 builds.
- Source: [NHS England Digital alert CC-4856](https://digital.nhs.uk/cyber-alerts/2026/cc-4856)

**Additional deployment-specific update: LibreOffice**

Seven LibreOffice 26.2.5 issues, CVE-2026-63272, CVE-2026-63273, CVE-2026-63274, CVE-2026-63275, CVE-2026-63276, CVE-2026-63278, and CVE-2026-63279, cover document-triggered buffer overflows, an out-of-bounds read, and possible environment/INI-value exfiltration. The vendor announcement is dated 21 September without a publication time; the advisory records surfaced on 22 September, so this is retained as a boundary item. Vendor severity was not stated. [LibreOffice security advisories](https://www.libreoffice.org/security/)

**Possible matches needing review**

Canonical also issued several 22 September notices for specialized Ubuntu kernel flavors, including Azure CVM, AWS, NVIDIA, Raspberry Pi, and low-latency kernels. These contain many previously assigned CVEs and are relevant only where those exact kernel packages are deployed. Review the [Ubuntu Security Notices index](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices) against installed kernel flavors.

**MongoDB ecosystem verification**

The dedicated sweep checked MongoDB Server Community and Enterprise, mongod, mongos, Atlas and Atlas services, Ops Manager, Cloud Manager, Compass, mongosh, Database Tools, Kubernetes Operator, official drivers and connectors, BI Connector, Charts, Realm/App Services, official integrations, and major MongoDB-maintained libraries. No credible MongoDB-family advisory was published or updated inside this run's window; nearby MongoDB Server and driver findings dated 11-18 September were excluded as stale.

**Review priority**

Immediate review is recommended for Erlang/OTP TLS 1.3 use, Erlang SSH exposure, and any deployed ManageEngine ADSelfService Plus GINA client. Next, validate the applicable Ubuntu/OpenSSH/libssh2 package updates and Veeam version exposure.
